title: PNP considering to visit Sara Duterte over alleged threats
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Monday said it is willing to visit Vice President Sara Duterte to gather details about the threats she reportedly have received.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Monday said it is willing to visit Vice President Sara Duterte to gather details about the threats she reportedly have received.
At a press briefing, PNP spokesperson Police Brigadier General Allen Rae Co said the police are open to personally meeting with Duterte to establish the facts surrounding her allegations.

“If she wants that we will go, we will be the ones to go to her para po kunin ang kanyang statement or 'yung facts po or the threats that she is saying, ay very much willing to do so po ang Philippine National Police,” Co said during a press briefing.
(If she wants that we will go, the PNP is very much willing that we will be the ones to go to her to get her statement or the facts or the threats that she is saying.)
While the PNP can conduct a motu proprio investigation, Co said that authorities need to know the specific incident or alleged crime being reported.
He said the PNP had invited Duterte to submit evidence or documents supporting her claims.
“If you told us that a crime was committed against you, hindi po sinasabi kung what crime, hindi po namin masisimulan,” he said.
(If you told us that a crime was committed against you, they wouldn't tell us what crime, we couldn't start.)
Asked whether the PNP had monitored any threats against the Vice President, Co said authorities had not detected any direct threats against her.

Over the weekend, Duterte said she has five "documented threats" against her. Yet, she cannot present the threats amid her impeachment trial "because the prosecution maliciously withdrew the charge of grave threats."
Duterte also reiterated that she is concerned for her personal safety.

"When I say that I do not feel safe in this country, I speak not only for myself but also for the many Filipinos who have experienced, or fear experiencing, the failure of law enforcement to make this country a place where people can live with the assurance that their fundamental rights will be respected," she said.
In September, the PNP said Duterte has yet to report to the PNP any threat against her and her family. — RSJ, GMA News
